title: educated
meaning_vi: (adjective / verb (past)). được giáo dục, có hiểu biết

examples.en: Parents who are educated about nutrition tend to raise children with healthier eating habits.

title: instilling healthy habits
meaning_vi: hình thành thói quen lành mạnh

examples.en: Instilling healthy habits early in life greatly reduces the likelihood of chronic disease in adulthood.

title: well-rounded and wholesome diets
meaning_vi: chế độ ăn cân đối và lành mạnh

examples.en: Schools that serve well-rounded and wholesome diets help children develop lifelong healthy eating habits.

title: specifically designed for senior citizens
meaning_vi: được thiết kế riêng dành cho người cao tuổi

examples.en: Several local gyms now offer low-impact classes specifically designed for senior citizens.

title: suitable fitness programs
meaning_vi: các chương trình thể dục phù hợp

examples.en: Health authorities should promote suitable fitness programs that take the physical limitations of older adults into account.

title: tailored to the needs of older adults
term: tailored to the needs of older adults
pronunciation: /ˈteɪləd tə ðə niːdz əv ˈəʊldər ˈædʌlts/
meaning_vi: được điều chỉnh phù hợp với nhu cầu của người cao tuổi

examples.en: Nutrition guidelines tailored to the needs of older adults can help prevent malnutrition in later life.

title: abundant
meaning_vi: dồi dào, phong phú

examples.en: Health information is now so abundant online that many people struggle to tell fact from myth.

title: Cosmetic procedures
meaning_vi: các thủ thuật thẩm mỹ

examples.en: Cosmetic procedures such as rhinoplasty have become increasingly common among young adults.

title: get profits as a reward for their innovativeness
term: get profits as a reward for their innovativeness
pronunciation: /ɡet ˈprɒfɪts æz ə rɪˈwɔːd fə ðeə ˌɪnəʊˈveɪtɪvnəs/
meaning_vi: nhận lợi nhuận như phần thưởng cho sự sáng tạo

examples.en: Supporters argue that companies should get profits as a reward for their innovativeness in developing new vaccines.

title: profit incentive
meaning_vi: động lực lợi nhuận

examples.en: Critics claim that the profit incentive drives pharmaceutical firms to prioritise lucrative drugs over rare-disease treatments.

title: Complications
meaning_vi: biến chứng

examples.en: Doctors warned that complications from the surgery could include infection and prolonged recovery.

title: indulging in plastic beauty
meaning_vi: buông thả theo vẻ đẹp nhân tạo

examples.en: Indulging in plastic beauty without medical advice can lead to irreversible damage to one's skin.

title: poses physical and psychological risks
meaning_vi: gây ra những rủi ro về thể chất và tâm lý

examples.en: Undergoing repeated cosmetic surgery poses physical and psychological risks that patients often underestimate.

title: alleviate the symptom
meaning_vi: làm giảm triệu chứng

examples.en: The new medication does not cure the illness but can alleviate the symptoms significantly.

title: cure diseases
meaning_vi: chữa khỏi bệnh

examples.en: Scientists hope that gene therapy will eventually cure diseases that are currently considered untreatable.

title: evidence-based recommendations
meaning_vi: những khuyến nghị dựa trên bằng chứng khoa học

examples.en: National health bodies should issue evidence-based recommendations rather than relying on outdated guidelines.

title: money poured into medical treatment research
term: money poured into medical treatment research
meaning_vi: khoản tiền đổ vào nghiên cứu điều trị y tế

examples.en: The money poured into medical treatment research has led to significant breakthroughs in cancer therapy.

title: illicit markets
meaning_vi: thị trường chợ đen

examples.en: Excessive taxation on tobacco can inadvertently fuel illicit markets selling untaxed cigarettes.

title: purview
meaning_vi: phạm vi quyền hạn

examples.en: Setting the school lunch menu falls within the purview of the education ministry.

title: drive economic activity
meaning_vi: thúc đẩy hoạt động kinh tế

examples.en: Investment in transport infrastructure can drive economic activity, though it is not a substitute for healthcare funding.

title: economic prosperity
meaning_vi: sự thịnh vượng kinh tế

examples.en: A healthy workforce is widely seen as a prerequisite for sustained economic prosperity.

title: economically disadvantaged groups
meaning_vi: nhóm người có hoàn cảnh kinh tế khó khăn

examples.en: Sugar taxes may disproportionately burden economically disadvantaged groups who spend a larger share of income on food.

title: ensuring national security and defense
meaning_vi: đảm bảo an ninh quốc phòng

examples.en: Governments often justify limited healthcare spending by citing the need for ensuring national security and defense.

title: initiatives to stimulate economic growth
meaning_vi: các sáng kiến kích thích tăng trưởng kinh tế

examples.en: Critics claim that initiatives to stimulate economic growth are prioritised at the expense of public health funding.

title: require substantial financial resources
meaning_vi: đòi hỏi nguồn lực tài chính đáng kể

examples.en: Building a nationwide network of rural clinics would require substantial financial resources from the state budget.

title: take precedence over
meaning_vi: được ưu tiên hơn

examples.en: Some argue that infrastructure spending should take precedence over expanding public healthcare budgets.

title: tax breaks for businesses
meaning_vi: ưu đãi thuế cho doanh nghiệp

examples.en: Offering tax breaks for businesses may boost employment but does little to address rising healthcare costs.

title: tax revenue
meaning_vi: doanh thu thuế

examples.en: Tax revenue generated from tobacco sales can be redirected to fund public health initiatives.

title: wield
meaning_vi: nắm giữ, vận dụng (quyền lực)

examples.en: Regulatory bodies wield considerable influence over how food companies label their products.

title: serves as discrimination against the poor
term: serves as discrimination against the poor
meaning_vi: trở thành một hình thức phân biệt đối xử với người nghèo

examples.en: Opponents claim that a flat sugar tax serves as discrimination against the poor, who spend a larger share of income on food.

title: widening the gap between the rich and the poor
term: widening the gap between the rich and the poor
pronunciation: /ˈwaɪdnɪŋ ðə ɡæp bɪˈtwiːn ðə rɪtʃ ænd ðə pɔː/
meaning_vi: nới rộng khoảng cách giàu nghèo

examples.en: Unequal access to healthcare risks widening the gap between the rich and the poor even further.

title: curtailing
meaning_vi: hạn chế, cắt giảm

examples.en: Curtailing the advertising of sugary snacks to children is a key aim of the new regulation.

title: addressing the issue
meaning_vi: giải quyết vấn đề

examples.en: Addressing the issue of teenage smoking requires cooperation between schools, parents and the government.

title: be funded by governments
meaning_vi: được chính phủ tài trợ

examples.en: Basic scientific research should be funded by governments rather than left entirely to private companies.

title: collaborative approach
meaning_vi: cách tiếp cận mang tính hợp tác

examples.en: A collaborative approach between schools, families, and local governments is needed to tackle childhood obesity effectively.

title: complementary measures
meaning_vi: biện pháp bổ sung

examples.en: Complementary measures such as subsidies for fresh produce should accompany any sugar tax.

title: deter consumption
meaning_vi: ngăn cản việc tiêu thụ

examples.en: Higher taxes on alcohol are designed to deter consumption and reduce alcohol-related health problems.

title: developing an alternative
meaning_vi: phát triển một giải pháp thay thế

examples.en: Instead of banning junk food outright, some officials favour developing an alternative that is both healthy and affordable.

title: financial deterrent
meaning_vi: rào cản tài chính

examples.en: A sugar tax acts as a financial deterrent, discouraging consumers from buying sweetened beverages.

title: fulfill their responsibility
meaning_vi: hoàn thành trách nhiệm của mình

examples.en: Local authorities must fulfill their responsibility to provide clean drinking water for every household.

title: hiking the price
meaning_vi: tăng giá mạnh

examples.en: Hiking the price of sugary drinks is one strategy governments use to curb rising obesity rates.

title: imposing a tax on
meaning_vi: áp thuế lên

examples.en: Imposing a tax on sugary beverages has proven effective at reducing consumption in several countries.

title: mandating
meaning_vi: bắt buộc, quy định

examples.en: Mandating nutrition labels on packaged food helps consumers make more informed choices.

title: prosperous society
meaning_vi: xã hội thịnh vượng

examples.en: Reducing preventable illness is a cornerstone of building a genuinely prosperous society.

title: public health funding
meaning_vi: kinh phí y tế công cộng

examples.en: Increased public health funding is essential for expanding access to preventive care in poorer regions.

title: regulating the food environment
meaning_vi: điều chỉnh môi trường thực phẩm

examples.en: Regulating the food environment around schools has proven effective in reducing junk food consumption among teenagers.
